boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Wilmington record (February 12-22, 1865) in Operations Against Fort Fisher and Wilmington [January-February 1865]: the operations against Fort Anderson and the Sugar Loaf line, Town Creek and the evacuation of Wilmington. Schofield's February 11 advance and the January capture of Fort Fisher (NC015) fall outside the interval and are context; the March Kinston operations belong to another campaign and are not added. Loss totals for February 11-22 are context, not assigned to one day. The live NPS campaign dates (January-February 1865) do not replace the frozen interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to one record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field and imported bounds give Cox's, Ames's and Paine's divisions at 12,000 against Hoke's division and Hagood's brigade at 6,600; the live Forces Engaged field repeats 12,000 and 6,600, and NPS says about 6,600 Confederates under Hoke held Fort Anderson and a line of works. Schofield says Terry held a line with about 8,000 men when Cox's division landed on February 9, and that the force he then had seemed too small to turn the position. Bragg says Terry had been reinforced by Schofield's corps to nearly 20,000, that his own force of all arms did not exceed 6,500 effectives including reserves and cavalry, and that Hagood's Fort Anderson garrison was 2,000.
claims.rationale: Imported and reported figures with different bases and dates: the frozen bounds' basis is not stated, Schofield's 8,000 is Terry's force on February 9 before Cox's arrival, and Bragg's 20,000 and 6,500 are his February 25 figures. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; the live zeros are not measured absence. The frozen bounds are imported unchanged.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Schofield (Major General) and Bragg (General); the live page gives 'Major General Braxton Bragg', and the frozen ranks are kept. Schofield says he pushed Terry's line forward with Cox's division in support, crossed Cox's and Ames's divisions to Smithville, and that Cox routed the Town Creek position while Terry held Hoke's force. Bragg says he reached Wilmington on the 21st, after the west bank was lost, and withdrew the troops before daylight on the 22d; NPS says Bragg ordered the evacuation. Hagood fought his way to Wilmington from Fort Anderson.
claims.rationale: Roles attributed by opposing interested reports. Bragg was absent until the 21st by his own account. No listed commander receives automatic sole credit; Terry, Cox, Ames, Hoke and Hagood are named as attributed actors, not rated.

claims.value: The frozen result is a Union victory. Schofield says the enemy abandoned his works on both sides of the river during the night of February 19 (the compiler brackets '[18]'), that Cox routed the Town Creek position on the 20th taking 2 guns and 375 prisoners, and that Union troops entered Wilmington without opposition early on the 22d. NPS dates the Fort Anderson evacuation to the night of the 18th-19th. Bragg says the withdrawal was made successfully before daylight on the 22d and the pursuit was feeble.
claims.rationale: The Fort Anderson date differs between Schofield's text and the compiler's bracket and NPS; kept as recorded. Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty field reads 1,150 total; the live page reads zero. Schofield gives the Union loss from February 11 to the capture as about 200 killed and wounded, and the enemy's as not less than 1,000 killed, wounded and prisoners. Bragg says Hagood lost about 350 of his command in fighting his way back; Schofield's 375 Town Creek prisoners are above.
claims.rationale: Schofield's span begins on February 11, before the frozen interval; his enemy figure is an estimate. Bragg's 350 is one brigade's loss. The frozen 1,150 is not reconciled with these figures; the live zero is not measured absence. Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Cox's No. 254 and Ames's No. 235 reports (Volume XLVII, Part 1), Terry's and Hoke's reports if any, Porter's naval reports (Official Records of the Navies, Series I, Volume 12, whose Internet Archive OCR returned a server error on retrieval), Cox's history (chapter IX), the Kinston part of Schofield's report and Bragg's March dispatches (read, not selected), and maps remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Terry's reports (Official Records Series I, Volume XLVI, Part 1), Schofield's report (Volume XLVII, Part 1) and Bragg's reports (Volumes XLVI and XLVII, one author family) are separate families of interested participants' accounts; the volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Porter's naval reports, Whiting's January report and Cox's history (The March to the Sea, 1882, chapters VIII-IX, registered earlier) were not inspected under the three-family ceiling. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
